Thus common signed tau bound ceil(W/Q)+L(ell−1) and E=u+Nv−signR−Qtau. Only polylog carry inflation for allowed small ell. tasks.latestTerminalSummary:
The digit-cut identity is exact, and the fixed-carry terminal product is a real composite-ring algorithm. On the short balanced rectangle that recursion still pays the surviving pair count. No checked evaluator beats explicit pairs once a residual digit convolution remains. **Verified complete factoring improvement: NONE.** The one-sixth balance is not an algorithm.

The report is `research/findings/W030-digit-kernel-review.md`. Evidence, the frozen brief, and the prior-art scope are in `research/findings/W030-digit-kernel-review-evidence/`. Both earlier Opus rounds terminated with "Claude gave up after repeated API errors" and contributed no mathematics. The root-table audit and the parent's unbalanced-cost note were not re-opened.

The integer cut holds for canonical digits. The low block enters as the full product \(a_0b_0\), not as a truncated \(R_h\). Digits in the top \(h\) places drop out of the residual only; they still appear in the row-only and column-only labels. With the sign held fixed, the residual base is the unit \(\alpha^{B^2}\), and the carry stays a column scalar. At \(L=2h\) the bucket product is exactly \(\prod(1-r_is_j)\). Monic remainder trees compute one carry in \(\widetilde O(n+m)\) operations in \(\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\), and a carry progression on that same separable bucket costs \(\widetilde O(\sqrt{nmT}+n+m)\). Localization is a gcd descent of the same order.

Under the imported congruence, a prefix modulus at least as long as the coordinate interval makes each terminal bucket a single pair. The fast terminal bound then has both lengths equal to 1, so the recursion reproduces the filtered pair count. The earlier-prefix figures \(\min(U,B)\min(V,B)\) and \(U\min(V,B)+V\min(U,B)\) are upper bounds on this indexing. They are not a lower bound on other algorithms. Dense-box and \(2^b\) counts price those two implementations only.

Dense multipoint theorems were checked against their actual input: a coefficient tensor. For this block that tensor is the superpolynomial box \((b+1)((\ell-1)b+1)^L\). Cartesian resultants, sparse multipoint, and rank-\(L\) exponent factorizations do not remove it. The unsolved scalar is the joint bucket product whose labels depend on both prefixes and whose residual convolution still has positive precision.
